tests.name: Quick Check
tests.description: Timed check on Crime, Media & Public Perception

questions.question: Describe Cohen's concept of moral panics and evaluate its usefulness.
questions.correctAnswer: Cohen: moral panics occur when the media defines a group as a threat. Mods and rockers: media exaggerated violence, labelled them as folk devils, and the deviancy amplification spiral created more deviance. Evaluation: useful but some panics may reflect genuine concern.

questions.question: Explain how the media distorts the public's perception of crime.
questions.correctAnswer: The media distorts crime by: over-representing violent crime (12% actual, 60-70% media), under-representing corporate crime, using emotionally charged language. Result: public overestimates violent crime and underestimates white-collar crime.

questions.question: Evaluate whether media coverage of crime causes more harm than the crime itself.
questions.correctAnswer: Media harm: creates fear, diverts resources, drives punitive policy. Crime harm: direct damage to victims. Evaluation: both cause significant harm, but media distortion can be more harmful because it misdirects resources from effective prevention.
